import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# --- Data Preprocessing ---
# Combine date and time, then convert to datetime objects
df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'] + ' ' + df['time'])

# Extract the hour and the day of the week
df['hour'] = df['datetime'].dt.hour
df['day_of_week'] = df['datetime'].dt.day_name()

# --- Data Aggregation for Visualization ---
# Create a pivot table to sum total sales by day of the week and hour
sales_heatmap_data = df.pivot_table(
    values='total',
    index='day_of_week',
    columns='hour',
    aggfunc='sum',
    fill_value=0
)

# Ensure the days of the week are in chronological order
day_order = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday']
sales_heatmap_data = sales_heatmap_data.reindex(day_order)

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="white", font_scale=1.1)

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(18, 9))

# Generate the heatmap
heatmap = sns.heatmap(
    sales_heatmap_data,
    cmap='YlGnBu',
    linewidths=0.5,
    linecolor='lightgray',
    annot=False,  # Annotations would be too cluttered
    ax=ax,
    cbar_kws={'label': 'Total Sales ($)'} # Add a label to the color bar
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---
# Set the title with more context
ax.set_title(
    'Coffee Shop Sales Heatmap: Peak Hours by Day of the Week',
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight='bold',
    pad=25
)

# Set axis labels
ax.set_xlabel('Hour of the Day (24-hour format)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Day of the Week', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Improve tick label readability
plt.xticks(rotation=0, ha='center')
plt.yticks(rotation=0)

# Format the color bar ticks to show currency
cbar = ax.collections[0].colorbar
cbar.formatter = mticker.FormatStrFormatter('$%1.0f')
cbar.update_ticks()

# Adjust layout to make sure everything fits without overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
